title: Exchange, KIA & 2nd Moves
intro: Equalize comfortably in the Exchange Variation with ...Bd6 and ...Nf6, fight White's King's Indian Attack (2.d3) with ...d5 and ...c5, and meet 2.Nf3 or 2.c4 with 2...d5.
variation: e2e4 e7e6 d2d4 d7d5 e4d5, e2e4 e7e6 d2d3, e2e4 e7e6 g1f3, e2e4 e7e6 c2c4

steps.text: In the Exchange Variation, White clears the centre on move three.
Recapture with the pawn to open your c8 bishop.
steps.hint: Take back on d5 with the e-pawn.
steps.ifWrong: Play 3...exd5: both bishops develop freely now.
steps.ifRight: Black has zero pawn weaknesses and easy development.

steps.text: Put your dark-squared bishop on an active diagonal.
steps.hint: Develop the f8 bishop to d6.
steps.ifWrong: Play 4...Bd6 to control e5 and point at White's kingside.

steps.hint: Put the g8 knight on f6.
steps.ifWrong: Play 5...Nf6 (or 5...Ne7) so you can castle next.
steps.ifRight: Black castles next and brings the c8 bishop to g4.

steps.text: If White tries 4.c4 to attack your d5 pawn, defend it actively.
steps.hint: Develop your king's knight to defend d5.
steps.ifWrong: Play 4...Nf6 (followed by ...Bb4+ or ...Be7) to guard d5 and keep pace in development.
steps.ifRight: After 5.Nc3 Bb4, Black gets lively piece play.

steps.text: With 2.d3, White avoids open centre play and heads for a King's Indian Attack with Nd2, Ngf3 and g3.
Claim your share of the centre immediately.
steps.ifRight: Black takes space in the centre right away.

steps.text: Expand in the centre and prepare ...Nc6 before White settles.
steps.ifWrong: Play 3...c5 (or 3...Nf6) to claim the d4 square.
steps.ifRight: Black grabs space on the queenside and centre.

steps.text: Develop your queen's knight to control d4 and e5.
steps.hint: Put the b8 knight on c6.
steps.ifRight: Black has a harmonious set-up with extra central space.

lessons.title: Meeting 2.Nf3 and 2.c4
lessons.summary: Play 2...d5 against White's quieter second moves.

steps.text: If White delays d4 with 2.Nf3, Black still sticks to the French plan.

steps.ifRight: Now White must choose between 3.Nc3, 3.e5 or 3.exd5.

steps.text: White defends with 3.Nc3 (the Two Knights Attack).
Keep attacking e4 and transpose into healthy Classical lines.
steps.hint: Develop your king's knight to f6.
steps.ifWrong: Play 3...Nf6: if 4.e5 Nfd7, Black follows with ...c5.
steps.ifRight: After 4.e5 Nfd7, Black hits the centre with ...c5.

steps.text: What if White tries to prevent ...d5 with 2.c4?
steps.ifWrong: Play 2...d5: after 3.exd5 exd5 4.cxd5 Nf6, Black wins the pawn back with fast development.
steps.ifRight: Playing 2...d5 gives Black an active, comfortable game.

steps.text: White took twice on d5. Recapture cleanly instead of bringing the queen out early.
steps.hint: Develop your king's knight to attack d5.
steps.ifWrong: Play 4...Nf6 so you recapture with the knight and avoid losing time with the queen.
steps.ifRight: Black wins d5 back next with ...Nxd5 and stands very well.

feedback.d8d5: 4...Qxd5 allows 5.Nc3, chasing your queen with tempo. Play 4...Nf6.
